file_inventory.method: GraphQL pullRequests and fully paginated PullRequest.files at 100 paths per page. Every file count reconciled with changedFiles.

pages_checked.candidate_review: Screened the title, body and changed-file list of all 67 PRs. Read targeted file diffs for candidate repairs and compared base and head blobs where GitHub omitted patch text.
pages_checked.head_status: GraphQL last commit statusCheckRollup and registered check names, matched to the REST head SHA.

matching_prs.title: The message_id_conflict test checks the refused call's turn, so it no longer fails under load
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: Two turns could log the same tool after the test's marker. A successful first call sometimes satisfied the replay test's wait before the refused call completed.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Wait for the failed tool outcome before checking its error code and send history.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The wait predicate changed from matching `poppy_message` to `poppy_message:error`. The existing assertions on `message_id_conflict` and the replay stayed in place.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Wait for an observable outcome that uniquely identifies the action under test.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The eight repeat runs are author-reported. A successful head check establishes one recorded CI outcome.

matching_prs.title: Fix Poppy recovery, stale token reuse and discovery hangs
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: Generated histories could count activity without establishing its effects or owner. A generic error and an accumulated transition count could both look like a successful test.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Check completed transitions and state after each generated step. Add positive controls, exact refusal expectations and tests that deliberately corrupt the Python oracle's inputs.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The model requires a particular refusal code and status, an unchanged operation list, and per-history `assertTransitions`. The outbox test checks order, payloads and traversal counts for 100,000 messages. Python controls reject wrong owners and missing fixture data.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Give a generated test an independent expected outcome, verify that each prerequisite ran, and demonstrate that a known bad result fails.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The large backlog test measures input traversals. The larger local history and interoperability runs are described by the author.

matching_prs.title: Upgrade pi to 1.3.0 and let agents hibernate after each turn
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The existing fake OpenAI returned a single canned text message. It could accept histories a real reasoning provider would reject. The deployed SQLite adapter also lacked the library's own conformance checks.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Teach the fake to validate returned history across turns and run the upstream storage suite against the agent's SQLite, including beside existing application tables.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The fake now checks that tool calls are paired with their earlier reasoning. The lane asserts reasoning counts `[0, 1]` across two turns. `registerStorageConformance` runs twice and a separate check preserves host table contents.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Make provider doubles enforce the external contract and run a dependency's conformance suite on the real adapter.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The provider was simulated. The storage checks exercised the local Workers test runtime.

matching_prs.title: Fix agent isolation, authorization and recovery boundaries
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The calculator property treated every mathematically undefined result as proof that division by zero had to be the first runtime error. A bounded eager evaluator can encounter an oversized operand earlier.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Repair the independent reference check and keep fixed examples for both error orders.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The property now accepts an oversized-intermediate error only with an independent size witness above 3,000 bits. It explicitly fails if a division by zero produces a result. Four examples distinguish size-first and division-first evaluation.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: When several failures are valid, establish independent evidence for each allowed outcome and retain counterexamples for their ordering.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: This is a test-oracle repair within a wider application audit. The head CI status does not report an individual generated history.

matching_prs.title: Add Poppy 0.2 support while retaining 0.1 compatibility
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The interop harness could apply a legacy known-failure exemption to a new protocol version. A retry dropped both the version and specification revision that defined the original case.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Version the exemptions and preserve the complete protocol context on retry.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: An unversioned exemption defaults to 0.1. A regression rejects that exemption for a 0.2 failure and accepts an explicitly 0.2 exemption. The retry regression inspects both version and revision.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Include the dimensions that define a test case in its retry identity and in any expected-failure exception.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The PR records seven independent-peer compatibility failures in its wider grid. A green required job does not cover every possible peer pairing.

matching_prs.title: Test PDA against four live Poppy 0.2 Companies
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: The live runner stamped all peers as Poppy 0.1, including peers serving 0.2. A result could therefore be recorded under the wrong protocol.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Give a live entry an expected version and verify it during discovery before the session scenario proceeds.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The old manifest hard-coded `["0.1"]`. A regression gives a 0.2 case a peer declaring 0.1, expects an error, and checks that `discover` was the only adapter call.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Verify the observed peer version before running or labeling version-specific cases.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The signed-out live results reported in the PR cover selected steps. The live lane did not record wire traffic.

matching_prs.title: Add lenient, strict and sloppy fake Personal Agents; live-test Alpine and Print with Poppy
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: The grid varied Company behavior but had no honest agent profiles for comparison. A dropped registry environment also made nominally different live agents run the default code path.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Add strict, lenient and deliberately sloppy agent profiles, propagate the selected profile into the live container, and test attribution and permitted scenarios.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The live environment now includes `entry.env`. The new profile suite checks each declared reading, and attribution cases distinguish differences between an agent and a Company using a reference peer.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Exercise materially different peer implementations and make their effective configurations observable.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: These profiles share the PDA implementation. Independent interoperability evidence is limited to the external peers and scenarios actually run.

matching_prs.title: Move Print with Poppy's pin to 3360d8b, draft 0.2
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: The pinned store could not exercise current 0.2 sessions in the isolated grid. Its expected-failure list still contained retired 0.1 cases and an ordering exemption for a defect fixed upstream.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Restore a compatible isolated peer and remove the obsolete exemptions. Record the remaining expected refusal against its actual version and owner.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The adapter declares 0.2 and registers the two 0.2 SDK clients. The diff deletes the wildcard `OU` exemption for the store and restricts the remaining deliberately erroneous agent case to 0.2.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Reconcile expected failures with each fixture upgrade. Remove exemptions as soon as their scenario succeeds or becomes inapplicable.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The store runs in isolated demo mode. The evidence covers the pinned test integration.

matching_prs.title: Prove each run tests what it says: live identity pre-flight and manifest checks
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: Green runs had exercised the default agent under other profile names. A separate run reached a Company before discovering that its configured test identity was unavailable.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Check the public test identity before starting the grid and compare each running adapter's manifest with its registry entry.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: `manifestMismatch` checks profile, protocol, adversarial flag and live client identity. The tests accept matching manifests, reject mismatches, and check registered implementations and scenarios referenced by expected failures.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Check that the intended subject, identity and fixture are in place before a test result can count.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: Preflight verifies identity and configuration. Each scenario still needs its own behavioral assertions.

matching_prs.title: Classify unavailable live interop scenarios on Poppy 0.4
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: Live peers without optional services were counted as failures. Missing fixture inputs could lead the runner to execute part of a scenario it could never finish.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Check required fixture inputs before dispatch. Classify an absent live capability as unsupported, and retain failures for broken advertised behavior or a test adapter that promised it.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The same CL/ML cases now distinguish live absence from a capability claimed by the adapter. CLI regressions require `unsupported` with empty steps for incomplete fixtures and exercise a complete S0 fixture.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Record unsupported coverage separately from an exercised failure. Validate known prerequisites before any step executes.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: Open at the audit date. Synthetic peers exercise the classification and the PR reports no new live Company run.

matching_prs.title: Check our Company checks against flawed Companies; extend the official validator's lanes
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: The in-house conformance checkers could agree with an honest mock while missing real deviations. There was no inventory of which upstream checks they covered.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Run three clean baselines and ten single-flaw mock variants against both the official and local checkers. Validate the coverage inventory against the upstream catalogue.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The lane records which checker caught each fault. `FLAW_CASES` verifies that the switches alter the fixture. A catalogue test requires exactly the upstream check IDs in order and resolves each claimed local reference.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Test the checker itself with clean and deliberately incorrect examples. Preserve the list of faults only an independent checker catches.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The PR reports 50 of 74 upstream checks covered locally and three modeled flaws caught only upstream. Its local grid uses simulated Companies.

matching_prs.title: Fix approval races, company status mixups, and budget test expiry
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: A budget-admission test added spend for a fixed October date but pruned the ledger against the real clock. The test aged out of its seven-day window.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Pass the test's existing `now` through the fixture write so admission and retention use the same date.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The setup changed from `ledger.add(DAY, 0.1)` to `ledger.add(DAY, 0.1, now)`. The approval and UI regressions are separate changes in this PR.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Inject the same clock into every operation that creates, expires or reads a time-sensitive fixture.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The PR reports that restoring the old fixture reproduced the failure. The audit independently checked the diff and CI status.

matching_prs.title: Refresh ecosystem evidence and document component Poppy support
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The specification drift check aborted on an upstream 404, hiding subsequent results and conflating a removed schema with an unavailable service.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Classify a missing current schema as drift, continue comparing files, and keep other HTTP errors visible.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The test invokes the CLI in a child process with injected 404 and 500 responses. It checks the `REMOVED` output in the first case and the HTTP error in the second. Both exit with status 1.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Test the exit code and the reason a verification command failed. A shared nonzero code can hide different outcomes.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The automated regression injects HTTP responses. A live drift run is separately described in the PR.

matching_prs.title: Speak Poppy 0.3 only, and refuse Companies on 0.1 or 0.2
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The mock and independent Python client both dropped message context, so their agreement hid data loss. In-process recovery tests also lacked evidence from a real process death and an independently surviving peer.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Use the upstream kit against the mock, test the Python oracle against damaged echoes, and add real process-kill recovery checks backed by the Company's ledger.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The Python control requires absent or changed context to raise `AssertionError`. The crash script kills the actual worker process group and checks the separate Company's effect count and the stable notification identity after recovery.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Validate a test double against an independent implementation. Verify crash recovery at the process boundary with a durable witness outside the process.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The upstream kit's raw and separately adapted runs have different prerequisites. The crash scenarios use isolated local processes.

matching_prs.title: Use Company-driven Poppy 0.3 approvals and preserve checkout links
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: A privacy test changed authority after requesting a background alarm, before establishing that the target read had finished. It could inspect the wrong log history.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Wait for the signed-in read's actual refusal before signing out and checking logs. Use a held tool promise to test logging across the end of a turn.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: A new `until` predicate looks for `PoppyError` with `invalid_client` before the sign-out step. The new logger regression controls a pending tool with an explicit release promise.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Observe completion at the boundary the assertion depends on before changing the state under test.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The PR explicitly leaves the precise cause of the earlier CI privacy assertion unresolved. The logger race is a separate regression.

matching_prs.title: Upload task-selected photos without a redundant approval
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: A feedback retry test assumed the first of two concurrent calls reached the transport first. An asynchronous prerequisite made invocation order unreliable.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Hold the first transport call, wait until it has entered, admit the queued call, then release and assert the original outcomes.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The old `Promise.allSettled([sendFeedback(...), sendFeedback(...)])` became explicit `reached` and `held` promises. The `finally` block releases the barrier and restores the mock.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Use a barrier at the contested boundary to choose the interleaving a concurrency test intends to exercise.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The test covers a specific queue history. The PR reports that disabling queued rejection recovery made it fail.

matching_prs.title: Simplify project docs and select CI checks by changed files
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: Appendix A used literal test titles as references, so an innocuous rename broke the checker and required collecting the runtime suite to verify documentation.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Link to stable evidence files and scenarios. Replace the old title-discovery tests with tooling tests for valid and missing references.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The diff removes the old Vitest result/title collector and its tests. A new temporary-checkout fixture contains a deliberately changeable test title and checks both valid links and missing files.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Use a stable reference for documentation and test behavioral coverage in the executable suite.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: This match concerns brittle test-title discovery. File existence supports navigation and cannot establish that a requirement is exercised.

matching_prs.title: fix: preserve model-key replacements and align validation and docs
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The validator's nominal 2,048-bit RSA fixture was an arbitrary repeated character whose encoding was noncanonical. A fixture intended to represent valid input could enter a different validation branch.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Correct the fixture, reuse the old encoding as a rejection case and add real generated EC and RSA key controls.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The fixture changes from 342 identical characters to a canonical final character. The suite also generates public keys, exports them with `jose`, and tests their acceptance alongside targeted invalid inputs.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Validate positive fixtures with an independent implementation and turn invalid former fixtures into explicit negative controls.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The generated-key controls cover representative importable public keys. The broader documentation link checker is outside this match.

matching_prs.title: Follow Poppy 0.3 as of 3 November (upstream 7205250)
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The existing interop trace checker treated a server on a different host as unlisted even when a Company's declared OpenAPI document named it. A valid path could produce a false failure.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Derive the allowed server set from the observed discovery and specification exchanges. Exercise both a listed server and an unrelated destination in the same regression.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: `describedHosts` reads the servers from fetched, declared OpenAPI descriptions. The new test requires only the unrelated destination to produce a finding. The mock also verifies operator signatures independently of the agent's signer.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Build a trace checker from observed protocol evidence, and include a near-miss negative control alongside a valid case.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The external behavior is represented by recorded exchanges and an independent Python client. These checks do not cover every live implementation.

matching_prs.title: Support MCP 2026-07-28's stateless lifecycle beside 2025-06-18
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The existing session-isolation suite exercised a single stateful MCP lifecycle. It could no longer establish that cache separation held on both kinds of server when the client added stateless negotiation.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Run the existing isolation and reauthentication cases under old-only, new-only and dual-version configurations. Draw those server profiles in the independent Python model.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: `describe.each(LIFECYCLES)` replaces the old single-profile setup. Each profile specifies the expected handshake sequence, and the model checks the selected era against the configured server.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: When a new protocol mode changes how an existing invariant is achieved, run the invariant against the full supported mode matrix.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The matrix uses mock servers. The PR reports that 17 of 20 lifecycle cases failed with the old client restored.

matching_prs.title: Add explicit Company access and data controls that no Company can block
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The project lacked a repeatable public smoke check tying a passing result to the intended deployed revision. Existing feature tests could not establish what build was serving public traffic.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Add a read-only deployment preflight with provenance assertions and controlled examples of wrong or dirty builds.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The test changes the fake `/api/build-info` response to a dirty build and a mismatched commit and requires each run to reject. It also requires a passing public receipt to record `authenticatedJourneyVerified` as false.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Verify the deployed artifact's identity before assigning a smoke result to a release. State which user journeys the probe actually exercised.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The PR did not deploy this change. The preflight covers anonymous public endpoints, with authenticated workflows tracked separately.

matching_prs.title: Share the sign-in error contract instead of scanning constructors
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: The sign-in UI test discovered error codes by applying a regex to OAuth constructor calls. A source refactor could silently change the test matrix without changing the public contract.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Define the wire-code registry once, enforce a complete UI message map at compile time and render each registered and unknown code.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The diff deletes `readFileSync(...oauth.ts).matchAll(...)`. The rendered UI test checks the shared registry and fallback cases `toString`, `__proto__` and `future_error`.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Drive contract coverage from the declared public values and test unknown inputs through the same user-facing path.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The PR reports that restoring the previous lookup failed two fallback controls. Head CI passed.

matching_prs.title: Adopt three Poppy 0.4 client rules that 0.3 allows, and plan the 0.4 upgrade
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: An existing refresh regression returned metadata for one service at another service's derived metadata address. It relied on an invalid setup to get to the refresh behavior it purported to test.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Make the initial metadata identify the service being exercised and preserve the assertion that later refresh drops the old audience.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The initial stub changes from `metadata(RESOURCE)` to `metadata(SERVICE)` and the expected sequence changes from `[RESOURCE, null]` to `[SERVICE, null]`.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Keep setup fixtures valid for the contract under test so another validation failure cannot shadow the intended assertion.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: Closed without merge. GitHub returned no head check rollup. The PR's local test results are author-reported.

matching_prs.title: Pin the Poppy 0.4 draft and its kit beside 0.3
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: The specification checker assumed a single pin. It could not verify a frozen release alongside a moving draft or attribute changes in shared pages to the right version.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Verify each version's snapshot and kit separately. Expand the CLI drift regression to cover frozen pages, draft pages, shared content, and HTTP failure.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The old single missing-page case became a per-pin fixture. Tests cover a clean baseline, changed or removed pages, shared-page attribution and HTTP 500. The checker compares runtime pins with supported versions.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Version the test oracle, fixtures and drift rules together when maintaining frozen and evolving contracts.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The newer kit's baseline initially stopped at discovery and skipped downstream checks. A successful integrity check alone does not establish conformance.

matching_prs.title: Poppy 0.4: pin the draft and kit, check the agent against the kit, exact resource metadata
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: Workers tests relied on the project's own strict mock and validator to judge requests from its own agent. A shared mistake could pass both.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Capture the outbound structured payloads during ordinary Workers tests and validate them after each test against the pinned upstream kit's schemas.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: Teardown compares `kitSchemaErrors` with expected errors and reports both unexpected and missing errors. Controls enumerate applied schema names and send malformed payloads. The final diff maps both the 0.3 and 0.4 validators.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Run an independent oracle over the actual data emitted by existing tests. Test the oracle with deliberately invalid data and verify which categories it saw.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: Coverage is limited to payload types for which the upstream kit defines schemas. Credential-bearing form bodies are excluded. The final diff is broader than the original PR description.

matching_prs.title: Drop Poppy 0.3: speak 0.4 alone
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The independent state machines avoided several histories that the mock mishandled, including retrying a previously refused request. Existing checks could therefore pass while the fixture contradicted the protocol.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Model the previously avoided cases during the 0.4 migration, retain minimized examples in Python and TypeScript, and add tests of the new oracle rules.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: Both suites now check that a retried refused handoff stays refused and that `as_of_request` names only accepted work. Oracle tests feed inconsistent states and logs to the checker. Legacy-only checks were removed with 0.3 support.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Convert state-machine findings into small permanent examples, then allow those histories in the generator so nearby variants remain reachable.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The PR's local Python machine and TypeScript mock exercise related protocol readings. The separate website-operations gap was handled in #59.

matching_prs.title: Challenge a signed-out Session at the mock's operations endpoint (MOCK-4)
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: The mock treated an eligible signed-out user and a different user as the same invalid request. Existing state machines did not exercise the website operations endpoint.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Correct the mock's response and add a direct endpoint regression for eligible and ineligible callers, with and without an approval.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The regression checks 401 with a challenge for the same signed-out user, `invalid_request` for another user, and an unchanged operation with nothing performed. The old fixture returned 400 in the first case.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Test fixture behavior directly whenever the higher-level model cannot reach a contract branch, and assert both the intended response and absence of side effects.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The finding came from review of the fixture. The PR reports a failing revert control. The challenge's exact scope is a local policy choice.

matching_prs.title: Fix four 0.4 review findings, keep cards on reworded revisions, and pair Print with Poppy at 0.4
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The mock and its independent Python model shared the same wrong ownership rule. Both tied a signed-out operation to the original session and accepted that session after it signed in.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Correct both implementations and test a different session of the same user, the original session after sign-in, and another user.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The Python rule replaces `ms is op.session` with a check on current sign-in state. The oracle now accepts another signed-out session and rejects a signed-in one. A direct mock test covers the same distinctions.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Check the behavioral model against the source contract and exercise cases that distinguish superficially equivalent identities.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The direct mock test works below the file-upload path because that fixture keeps uploads session-local. The separate full journey proves a narrower path.

matching_prs.title: Run D and S0 against Print with Poppy's live sandbox: both pass
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: Discovery was the only live scenario enabled for the independent print sandbox. It could pass while signed-out session establishment or a public catalog read was broken.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Enable the existing signed-out S0 scenario specifically for that sandbox and supply its public catalog operation as fixture data.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The sandbox's `liveScenarios` changes from `[D]` to `[D, S0]`. The new `openapi_public` fixture names `getCatalog`. The PR records initial failures and a later successful run for the three honest agent profiles.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Distinguish a peer's discovery availability from a functioning session. Add a scoped, repeatable operation before claiming the latter.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The live results are dated reports in the PR. Required CI does not independently establish those live outcomes or any authenticated purchase.

matching_prs.title: Run every honest agent against Print with Poppy, follow the Company card in a browser, keep a not-ready answer across a restart
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: The external print peer had ten CI scenarios but only one agent profile, and the company-access approval card had no browser journey. The not-ready order path also lacked recovery coverage at its waiting point.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Expand the existing CI matrix to all three honest agents, drive the card from the browser, and exercise a restart while the follow-up is waiting.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The same ten required scenarios now run with `pda,lenient-personal-agent,strict-personal-agent`. The recovery test waits for the persisted intent and verifies a completed order and a single approved request.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Run materially different clients against the same independent peer. Put recovery tests at the boundary between durable and in-memory progress.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The CI peer is a pinned demo store. The reported browser journey uses a synthetic Company.

matching_prs.title: Test an authorization event with its challenge on a successful response (8.11)
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: The requirement ledger pointed to a deleted test file that had never exercised an authorization challenge on a successful response. The existing implementation could have regressed unnoticed.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Make the mock actually send the header on a successful authorization event and check the client in both JSON and streamed-read configurations.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The test requires at least one successful recorded response carrying the challenge, one sign-in prompt, one message and one conversation, and no HTTP error. The old client behavior needed no production change.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Verify that a cited requirement test actually creates the condition it claims, then assert the outcome and cardinality of side effects.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The PR reports that making the client refuse challenges on every status fails both cases. No independent live Company exercised this behavior.

matching_prs.title: Speak the 1.0 draft beside 0.4
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: Adding a new default made the existing discovery grid stop exercising the older supported profile. The Python model also reused a user's newest key for older grants even when a grant retained its own key.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Add a dedicated 0.4 peer to the matrix, select the upstream schema by negotiated version and retain the issuing key in the test model for each bound grant.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: The runner test pins the older peer's `INTEROP_MOCK_VERSION` to 0.4. `refresh_key(grant)` replaces lookup of the user's current key on refresh. Each grant records its associated key.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Keep old supported configurations explicit in CI and bind the model's expected state to the object that owns it.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: This was the 1.0 draft. The published text and corresponding checks changed again in #75.

matching_prs.title: Quote the pinned sentence behind each check
matching_prs.classification: Direct test-quality or conformance-harness work
matching_prs.weakness: Coverage bookkeeping checked whether changelog entries had a disposition but never compared the checker with the requirement it enforced. Outdated MUST assertions survived after the specification changed to SHOULD.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Attach a pinned sentence to each normative validator message and mock check, verify that sentence and its keyword for each applicable version, and correct stale findings.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: A test quotes the old MUST sentence and gets a mismatch against the revised pin. Another rejects a SHOULD sentence presented as a MUST. The validator regression updates the scope finding's severity.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Keep the exact versioned requirement beside a conformance assertion and test the guard using historical wording that would give the wrong verdict.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The mechanical check covers pinned Poppy text. The PR documents additional behavior requiring review and external standards outside the quote checker.

matching_prs.title: Pin published Poppy 1.0 and verify final behavior
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: The strict mock and trace checker retained a draft assertion lifetime under final 1.0. An attribution test even searched source strings for a chosen threshold. Upstream probe prerequisites also varied by profile.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Apply the negotiated final rule to boundary values in mock and trace tests, check compatibility by behavior, and verify the separately adapted upstream probe on both pins.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: Tests accept lifetimes of 60, 120 and 300 seconds and flag 301. The source-regex assertion on `MAX_ASSERTION_LIFETIME` is removed in favor of compatibility cases. The CI workflow preserves raw and prerequisite-supplied results.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Verify a versioned public rule with boundary examples in every checker. Preserve raw upstream findings when an adapted run supplies missing prerequisites.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: The unmodified kit still reported a failure and warnings on certain profiles. The PR distinguishes those from results with prerequisites supplied.

matching_prs.title: Validator: report who answered a fetch; name the validator and agent to Companies
matching_prs.classification: Test-quality repair embedded in broader work
matching_prs.weakness: An activity test directly wrote conversation state while a long-running background read was still able to overwrite it. The asserted display depended on which writer finished first.
matching_prs.attempted_remedy: Wait for the in-flight read to finish and remove its idle job before the test takes ownership of the conversation row.
matching_prs.diff_evidence: A new `until` loop deletes only this conversation's `read-*` job when `running = 0`, then confirms the job is absent before the SQL fixture update and original display assertions.
matching_prs.transferable_rule: Give the test exclusive control of mutable fixture state by synchronizing with the actual background writer.
matching_prs.verification_caveat: Open at the audit date. The passing head check establishes CI status but cannot measure the remaining long-term flake rate.

exclusions.reason: These PRs diagnose pre-existing failing tests without repairing them in their diffs. #1 reports the flaky replay assertion later repaired in #6. #8 and #33 identify fixed-date budget failures. #14 and #32 contain clock repairs.

Their test edits accompany product changes or adjust assertions to updated behavior. #63 adds a currency property and delayed-checkout fixtures for its new handling. #74 factors shared directives to support a new provider. #72 reports a throwaway test and changes no committed tests.

Documentation, deployment observations, historical results or links to existing practice. #28 explains tamper cases, an inventory of checks and an independent Python client. It changes no test or conformance mechanism. #76 reruns the existing matrix with a temporary pin.
External specification research and snapshot extraction. #27 grades issues in the upstream protocol's text. The extractor changes capture revised source pages.
Diagnostic artifact retention and workflow dependency pin enforcement, respectively. The test assertions and conformance approach are unaffected.
Independent peer revision updates and historical evidence. #61 also updates an expected link to follow the new documentation. Neither changes scenario checks or the test method.

limitations: The unit of counting is the PR. Stacked upgrade PRs have overlapping diffs. Entries cite the change attributable to each proposal.

GitHub withheld some patch bodies on #36, #41 and #58. The complete changed-file inventories were available. Base and head file contents were compared for all 42 nonempty affected paths outside vendored snapshots and documentation directories, including 12 test paths on #36. Two empty marker files had no patch.

The review used historical source and GitHub check metadata. Suites, live services, wider optional matrices and author-reported revert experiments were not independently rerun. Green rollups cover the configured checks at the recorded head.

Large vendored protocol snapshots, generated captures and documentation-only receipts were screened by filename and context. The evidence quotes representative first-party changes, rather than every line in those inputs.
